raw_problem: Activation functions evolved from sigmoid and ReLU to GELU and gated units such as SwiGLU, which now dominate Transformer feed-forward layers. What open problem in activation-function design for Transformers is worth researching next, and how would we test it?
research_question: Which properties of the feed-forward activation in Transformers (gating, smoothness, sparsity, learnability) account for quality differences between ReLU, GELU and GLU-style units, and which under-explored property offers the best next research target?
motivation: Feed-forward layers hold most Transformer parameters and compute, and their activation is usually chosen by convention (GELU, then SwiGLU) rather than by understanding. Knowing which property drives the gains would turn activation design from trial-and-error into a targeted search, and could trade quality against efficiency such as activation sparsity.
in_scope: efficiency effects of the activation (sparsity, inference cost)
out_of_scope: activations for spiking or analogue hardware
inclusion_criteria: proposes, analyses or compares activation functions used in Transformer or language-model feed-forward layers
reports quality, training-dynamics or efficiency results
or is a primary source for an activation now used in Transformers (GELU, Swish, GLU)
